content: Cobicistat and azithromycin can each increase the levels of the other by interfering with the metabolism of the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. It is recommended to avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. Consider alternative antibiotics when cobicistat is coadministered with atazanavir or darunavir. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of bedaquiline by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors should not be coadministered with bedaquiline for more than 14 consecutive days unless the benefits outweigh the risks. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of bosentan by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction of bosentan is required. Similarly, darunavir increases bosutinib levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of brigatinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration with a strong CYP3A inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the brigatinib dose by 50%. After discontinuing the inhibitor, resume the previously tolerated brigatinib dose. Darunavir increases bromocriptine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination should be avoided or replaced with an alternative drug. Cobicistat increases cabozantinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If necessary, reduce the cabozantinib dose and resume the previous dose 2–3 days after discontinuing the inhibitor. Darunavir increases cabergoline levels by reducing its metabolism, making this combination contraindicated. Similarly, darunavir increases calcitriol levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Cobicistat increases capivasertib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the capivasertib dose and monitor for adverse effects. Carbamazepine decreases cobicistat levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs, and monitor for virologic response if coadministration is necessary. Darunavir increases ceritinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Ceritinib also increases darunavir levels, potentially leading to toxicity. Cobicistat and ceritinib together may increase toxicity and QT prolongation. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Chloramphenicol increases darunavir and cobicistat levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Cimetidine increases darunavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Cobicistat and clarithromycin increase each other's levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Clarithromycin also increases cobicistat levels. Darunavir increases colchicine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid colchicine with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, especially in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. Darunavir decreases conjugated estrogen levels through an unspecified mechanism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Darunavir and cobicistat increase copanlisib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration with strong CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the copanlisib dose to 45 mg. Cobicistat increases crizotinib levels, which may result in QT prolongation. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the crizotinib dose to 250 mg daily. Darunavir increases dabrafenib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Cobicistat increases daridorexant levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Darunavir increases diazepam levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use alternatives if available. Dexamethasone decreases cobicistat levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Long-term use of corticosteroids metabolized by CYP3A may increase the risk of systemic corticosteroid effects, including Cushing syndrome and adrenal suppression. Cobicistat increases dihydroergotamine levels, making this combination contraindicated. Darunavir increases dofetilide levels, which may lead to QT prolongation and cardiac arrhythmias. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Cobicistat increases doxorubicin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Darunavir increases edoxaban levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Dose adjustments may be required for DVT/PE treatment but not for NVAF. Efavirenz decreases darunavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs, as coadministration may result in loss of therapeutic effect and resistance. Efavirenz also decreases cobicistat levels. Cobicistat increases elacestrant levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Darunavir increases elbasvir/grazoprevir levels, making this combination contraindicated. Patients should not take antiretroviral medications for at least one month before initiating stem cell mobilization therapy and until all apheresis cycles are completed, as these drugs may interfere with the manufacturing of apheresis cells. Cobicistat increases encorafenib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the encorafenib dose to one-third of the original dose. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inhibitor. Darunavir increases entrectinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Similarly, darunavir increases enzalutamide levels, while enzalutamide decreases darunavir levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Cobicistat increases erdafitinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor closely for adverse reactions and consider dose adjustments. Darunavir also increases erdafitinib levels. Darunavir increases ergoloid mesylate levels by decreasing metabolism, making this combination contraindicated. Cobicistat and erythromycin increase each other's levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Darunavir increases erythromycin levels, making this combination contraindicated. Cobicistat increases eslicarbazepine acetate levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs, and monitor for virologic response if coadministration is necessary. Darunavir decreases synthetic conjugated estrogen levels through an unspecified mechanism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Cobicistat increases eszopiclone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Cobicistat increases etravirine levels, while etravirine decreases cobicistat levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Etravirine also decreases darunavir levels, potentially leading to resistance. Darunavir increases everolimus levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Darunavir increases fedratinib levels. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the fedratinib dose to 200 mg daily. Cobicistat increases fentanyl levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is necessary, monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust the fentanyl dose as needed. Darunavir decreases fexinidazole levels, while fexinidazole increases darunavir levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Fexinidazole inhibits CYP3A4, increasing the risk of adverse effects. Cobicistat increases futibatinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs, as coadministration may increase toxicity. Cobicistat increases gilteritinib levels. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for adverse effects and adjust the dose as needed. Darunavir increases glasdegib levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs, and monitor for QT prolongation if coadministration is necessary. Darunavir increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels, making this combination contraindicated. Cobicistat increases guanfacine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Cobicistat increases ibrutinib levels. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Idelalisib increases darunavir levels, while cobicistat increases idelalisib levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs, and monitor for toxicity if coadministration is necessary. Indinavir increases cobicistat levels, making this combination contraindicated. Darunavir increases infigratinib levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Cobicistat increases infigratinib levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Itraconazole increases cobicistat levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration.
